fy_label_note: Baba FY labels equal company fiscal years: KNF is calendar-year (spun from MDU 2023-05-31, so FY2021-FY2022 are carve-out history). Margin = VA consensus-pivot 'ebitda' / 'revenue' (adjusted basis). Window: peak FY2024 (15.97%) to trough FY2026E (15.11%, consensus; Q2 2026 actual 14.9% vs 16.9%). FY2025 actual was 15.78%. Peer offsets: VMC, MLM, CRH and GVA are calendar years. EXP's FY ends in March, so FY2026 ended March 2026 and is actual. ROAD's FY ends September 30.

company.inputs: FY2024 EBITDA 463.0M on revenue 2,899.0M; FY2026E 523.830M on 3,466.059M. FY2021 12.47%, FY2022 12.36%, FY2023 15.28%, FY2025 15.78% (496.5M / 3,146.0M). LTM 15.2% = TTM 6/30/26 company-reported $501.6M / $3,307.5M (document_id 223848, per the stage 3 record). Revenue growth includes the Strata acquisition (closed 2025-03-07) and bolt-ons.

peers.excluded: Non-US cement producers in the comps list dropped. ACA (Arcosa) skipped as more diversified; the peer set is capped at six.

attribution_ratio_note: (23.6076 - 25.3662) x 100 / 85.7895 = -2.0498. The ratio is negative because the peer median margin rose 176 bps while KNF's fell 86 bps. Five of six peers expanded; only EXP (cement) declined. On actuals only (FY2024 to FY2025) the picture is the same: KNF fell 19 bps while every peer except EXP expanded. The paving contractors most like KNF's contracting segment (ROAD, GVA) expanded too, despite similar diesel and asphalt exposure.

deciding_facts: Peers expanded while KNF contracted: peer median EBITDA margin rose 176 bps FY2024 to FY2026E (ratio -2.05), including paving contractors ROAD and GVA, and KNF's gap to the median widened from -764 to -1,025 bps.

Margin fell on rising revenue (+19.6%, Strata and bolt-ons). Management's own Q2 2026 bridge includes a mix shift to 'lower margin' asphalt paving, and the FY2025 margin-expansion guide (+20 to 70 bps) was missed.
confidence_note: This is mix and M&A execution, not an operating breakdown. The decline is small (86 bps, partly a FY2026 estimate). Some of the drivers are genuinely external (diesel, with recovery via escalators lagging one to two months; Texas rain; the Alaska winter). Aggregates pricing was +8%. There is also no cyclical compression to reverse: FY2026E 15.11% is still above FY2021-FY2022 (about 12.4%), and the 20% goal is new territory, not a recovery. The GXO-style framing does not fit.
